To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formation and emission of tetralalkylammoniun salt ions from a gelatin substrate is a function of the mass and concentration of the organic salt.

(1) ionization efficiencies decrease as mass of the tetraalkyl ammonium cation increases, (2) sputter-induced chemical damage accumulates faster for heavier cations, and (3) lower mass salts in gelatin matrices are suppressed at high salt concentrations.
the relative cation intensites are not a simple function of salt mass and that the desorption yields of salts decrease with increasing mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the matrix and the dopant on the formation and emission of tetralalkylammoniun salts sputtered from gelatin.
the formation and emission of intact tetraalkyl ammonium cation molecular species from a gelatin sample matrix.
the formation and emission of organic molecular ions sputtering from a gelatin sample matrix.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation and emission of tetramethylammonium salt cations from a gelatin sample matrix is not a function of the mass of the cations but rather the mass of the salt.
the formation of tetraalkymammonium salt cations is dependent on the salt mass.
the formation of intact organic salt cations from gelatin matrices depends on a combination of ion-molecule interactions, ionization efficiencies, and desorption efficiencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sputter yields decrease with increasing salt mass.
the desorption yields of tetraalkyammonium salts from a gelatin substrate decrease with increasing mass of cation.
the formation of tetraalkymmonium cations from a gelatin salt matrix is mass dependent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of tetraalkymonium salts in gelatin is highly sensitive to mass.
the formation and emission of tetramethylammonium cation molecular ions from a gelatin sample matrix is more efficient than that for the heavier tetraalkylated ammonium salts.
the formation of tetraalkymammonium salt cations from a gelatin sample matrix is a complex process involving a number of interrelated effects.
